The startup check only looks for a saved token and does not confirm it is still valid.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup for sign-in
sections.what: Brings in the store library, secure storage, the user and login response types, and the API client.
sections.why: Standard setup at the top of the file.

sections.name: AuthState
sections.title: What the sign-in state holds
sections.what: Lists the user, whether they are signed in, the loading flag, the biometric session ID, and the actions for each sign-in, sign-up, password reset and logout step.
sections.why: Gives one place that describes every sign-in method.
sections.watch_out: Every method that starts a session returns the same login response, so changing that shape affects all of them.

sections.name: useAuthStore (part 1)
sections.title: Email, phone and social sign-in
sections.what: Starts with no user and loading on. Defines email and password sign-up and sign-in, phone code sign-in, and Google or Apple sign-in. Each sends its request and then saves the returned tokens.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared save step keeps token handling in one place.
sections.watch_out: If saving the tokens fails after the server accepts the sign-in, the server holds a session that the app does not have.

sections.name: useAuthStore (part 2)
sections.title: Biometric, password reset, logout and startup check
sections.what: Handles biometric sign-in, password reset, logout and the startup check. Biometric sign-in currently sends a fixed placeholder text instead of a real check. Logout clears the tokens even if the server call fails. The startup check only looks for a saved token.
sections.why: Likely reason: logout should clear the device even when the server cannot be reached.
sections.watch_out: The server receives only a fixed text string for biometric sign-in, so it does not prove who is holding the phone.

summary: Holds who is signed in, and handles each sign-in, sign-up, sign-out and password reset step.
purpose: Lets screens sign users in and out and check whether a session exists.
why: Likely reason: all sign-in methods share one step that saves the tokens.
how: Starts with no user and loading on. Each sign-in method sends its request to the server, then saves the returned tokens and the user. Logout clears the tokens even if the server call fails. The startup check only looks for a saved token.
inputs: Email and password, phone and one-time code, Google or Apple identity tokens, and a biometric key.
outputs: Saved tokens, the signed-in user, and server calls.
risks: Biometric sign-in sends a fixed placeholder string instead of a real fingerprint or face check. The startup check does not confirm that the saved token still works.
debug: If sign-in succeeds but the app stays signed out, check the token-saving step and the saved key names. If biometric sign-in works without a real check, that is the placeholder. If the app shows signed in but calls fail, check the startup check.
